narrative.overview:
The site is a map you cross, not a stack of pages. Its three sections follow the colors of a flag, left to right: about (green), work (white), media (red). The whole stage takes the color of the section you are in, and a thin band of flag fields in the sticky header shows where you stand and where you can go. Moving between sections is a wipe along the flag, in the direction of travel.

The voice is casual, rigorous and quiet, "engineer, not tinkerer". The casual lives in the type: monospace throughout, with a variable axis that softens letterforms toward handwriting. The rigor lives in the structure: one grid, one spacing scale, one semantic color set that resolves per section.
keyCharacteristics: Stage color is the navigation state: green, paper or red fills the page, tinted near-black in dark scheme.
Monospace everywhere, two families, three roles.
Flat and borderless. Depth is never simulated.
One marker (the accent bar in the flag band) is the only chrome element that moves within a section.
Every motion has a reduced-motion answer; content degrades to plain readable routes.

rules.name: The Stage Rule
rules.body: The page background is the section. Never introduce a second background color for cards, panels or code blocks; surfaces are the stage itself.

rules.name: The Semantic Only Rule
rules.body: Components use --bg, --fg, --accent, --muted, --line, never the raw palette.

rules.name: The Accent Is Foreground Rule
rules.body: In light scheme the accent is the text color; only in dark does the accent become a hue (the glow).

rules.name: The Brightness Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Rank in navigation is carried by size and brightness, not hue.

rules.name: The Lean Rule
rules.body: A headword leans -15° into cursive on hover or focus, letter by letter, only on devices that really hover. Weight never changes.

rules.name: The No Border Rule
rules.body: No borders, rules or outlines as decoration. The only outline is the 2px accent focus ring.

dos: Do let the stage color follow the section, and fade it over 600ms (200ms under reduced motion) where view transitions don't run.
Do use semantic color tokens and spacing roles (gap-group, mt-section) from the UnoCSS preset, not raw values.
Do give every motion a reduced-motion answer: the color change still reads, the movement goes.
Do keep icon-only controls labelled via aria-label and title, with touch targets at least 30px.
Do use ease-out (cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)) for entrances and ease-in-out (cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1)) for things that move across the screen.
donts: Don't add borders, drop shadows, cards or rounded corners.
Don't introduce a hue outside the flag palette, or a color that doesn't resolve per section and scheme.
Don't use text="…" attributify on <a> or NuxtLink; it overwrites the link label.
Don't use Nahuatl as a visual motif, and don't invent words, pronunciations or meanings; they come from the owner.
Don't animate the weight axis; only slant, casual and cursive move.
